references.text: Sarai gives her maidservant Hagar to Abram as a wife, parallel to Leah giving her maidservant Zilpa to Jacob.
Laban gives his maidservant Zilpa to Leah at her marriage to Jacob, who is later given to Jacob as a wife by Leah.
Rachel gives her maidservant Bilhah to Jacob as a wife, parallel to Leah's action with Zilpa.
The action in the source text (giving Zilpa) receives its theological meaning through this verse's interpretation of 'wages'.
Human response to infertility (30:9) is set in perspective by God's sovereign intervention (29:31).
Parallel action (Laban gives a maidservant) that creates a clear pattern for both sisters.
